_README: Statement-wave assignments for v2 rows authored after X1 reconciliation. build_v2_manifest.py merges these rows into the manifest, assigns phase/repo/formal_name/source-verification metadata, and drives the statement=done overlay entries. Opt-in per-row hash pin (plan WP3): `source_hash` records the corpus statement text the second reader actually read, and `source_verified_by`/`source_verified_at` override the file/wave-level values for that row. build_v2_manifest.py exits with "source text changed since verification; re-verify" when the upstream text is later reworded, so a silent corpus edit can never leave a statement leg `done`.

axv_2307_15512_00.note: Erde-Kang-Lehner-Mohar-Schmid Conjecture 1.4: the cop number of a connected k-uniform hypergraph on n vertices is O(sqrt(n/k)). The cops-and-robbers game is defined locally in the new shared foundation hypergraph-theory/theories/foundations/hypergraph.v as a finite-horizon cop-win closure on positions: [hg_win E m C r] is a Boolean fixpoint on the number of remaining rounds (cops move first along [hg_move] = stay or step to a vertex of a common hyperedge, catching the robber the instant one lands on him; then the robber moves the same way), [hg_cop_win E c] existentially quantifies the placement and the horizon, and [hg_is_cop_number E c] says c cops win and no fewer do. Structurally the same shape as the graph game written concurrently in graph-theory-misc (no dependency between the packages). O(sqrt(n/k)) is a single absolute constant C quantified outermost, squared to clear the root: c^2 * k <= C^2 * n. Guards: 0 < k and k <= #|T| (the edgeless one-vertex hypergraph is vacuously k-uniform for every k and would refute the unguarded body; every hypergraph with a hyperedge satisfies k <= n, see grounding_X217.v).

X217:hypergraph-theory.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-09-23: 1/1 PASS. axv_2307_15512_00: the paper's Section 1.1 game rules were checked against hg_win -- players alternate with the cops moving first, pieces move along hyperedges (from u to any v sharing a hyperedge, hg_move; 'not every piece must be moved in every turn' = the stay disjunct), the cops win as soon as one occupies the robber's vertex, and the cop number is the least number of cops with a winning strategy (hg_is_cop_number). The finite-horizon existential is the standard winning condition on a finite position space. O(sqrt(n/k)) is one absolute C quantified outermost and squared to c^2 * k <= C^2 * n, which is the reading the paper itself needs when it observes that the conjecture implies Meyniel's at k = 2. The guard k <= #|T| has teeth (the edgeless one-vertex hypergraph is vacuously k-uniform for every k and would refute the unguarded body) and removes no genuine k-graph. Taking the cop number as a hypothesis does not weaken the statement: at most one c satisfies it and some c always wins (hg_cop_win_card).

axv_2401_00359_01.note: Fox-Sankar-Simkin-Tidor-Zhou Conjecture 6.2: for each k a constant c_k > 0 with ex(n,H) <= O_H(n^{k - c_k/d_max(H)}) for every k-uniform k-partite H. EXPONENT CLEARED TO NAT FORM by raising to the power d_max and multiplying through: (hg_turan F k n)^(hg_dmax F k) * n^ck <= K * n^(k * hg_dmax F k), eventually in n, with c_k depending only on k and the O_H constant K chosen after H. New shared vocabulary: [hg_containsb] (injective, non-induced copy of a pattern), [hg_turan F k n] (max hyperedges of an F-free k-uniform hypergraph on 'I_n), [hg_degeneracy] (least d such that every non-empty vertex set spans a vertex of degree <= d, via ex_minn), [hg_skeleton E i] (the (i+1)-sets inside a hyperedge), [hg_skel_degeneracy] = d_i, [hg_dmax E k] = max over 1 <= i < k. Guards: F != set0 (else d_max = 0 and the cleared inequality degenerates to n^ck <= K, refutable: grounding_X225.v) and 2 <= k (the paper says k >= 3; k = 2 is the Furedi / Alon-Krivelevich-Sudakov theorem).

axv_2401_00359_02.note: Fox-Sankar-Simkin-Tidor-Zhou Conjecture 6.4: ex(n,H_L) = n^{3-Theta(1/d)} for the 3-uniform 3-partite hypergraph H_L of a d x d Latin square. Theta(1/d) is rendered with two ABSOLUTE constants a, b > 0 quantified outermost (independent of d and of L) and both inequalities are cleared by raising to the power d without any truncated subtraction: n^(3*d) <= ex^d * n^a (lower) and ex^d * n^b <= n^(3*d) (upper). axv_2208_06858_02.note: Alon-Friedgut-Kalai-Kindler Conjecture 2.6, graph form of Levine's hat problem: lim_t lim_n alpha-bar(K(n)^{box t}) = 0. New local vocabulary in X227.v: [x227_kneser n] (Kneser graph on {set 'I_n}, distinct subsets adjacent iff disjoint - the x != y guard is what makes it irreflexive) and [x227_box_power G t] (t-fold Cartesian power on base's [cartesian_product], with 'K_1 as the empty power). The independence number is coq-graph-theory's [alpha]; the RATIO is kept division-free as q * alpha <= #|V| for eps = 1/q. The iterated limit is rendered 'forall q > 0, exists T, forall t >= T, exists n0, forall n >= n0', i.e. the outer limit over the inner LIMSUP, so no existence claim about the inner limit is smuggled in.

X227:homomorphism-theory.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-09-23: 1/1 PASS. axv_2208_06858_02: K(n) is the paper's Kneser graph on the WHOLE cube (all subsets of 'I_n, the empty set included and adjacent to every other vertex), distinct vertices adjacent iff their supports are disjoint -- checked against the paper's own sentence; x227_box_power with 'K_1 as the empty power is the Cartesian (Hamming) power, and G^box 1 = cartesian_product 'K_1 G is a copy of G, so alpha and #|V| are the intended ones. The iterated limit is rendered as 'forall q > 0, exists T, forall t >= T, exists n0, forall n >= n0', i.e. the outer LIMIT over the inner LIMSUP: the outer quantifier is the strong 'exists T, forall t >= T' (not the weaker 'exists t') and nothing asserts that the inner limit exists. bm_003.note: Halin 1970 (Bondy-Murty Appendix A #3), status DISPROVED (Bowler-Erde-Heinig-Lehner-Pitz 2017, Theorem 1.6): hypomorphic infinite graphs embed in each other. Authored faithfully as a refutation target; NO refutation is committed. Carrier is igraph.v's Prop-level [iGraph] with its [infinite_graph] (Dedekind infiniteness). New local vocabulary in X216.v: [x216_embeds] (isomorphism onto a NON-induced subgraph), [x216_del_iso] (G - v isomorphic to H - w, stated on the ambient vertex types so that no eqType is needed) and [x216_hypomorphic]. mathcomp-classical (cardinality.v's countable / #<=) was deliberately NOT used: its predicates go through boolp.asbool, which would make every Print Assumptions report the three classical axioms.

X216:infinite-graph-theory.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-09-23: 1/1 PASS. bm_003: 'isomorphic to a subgraph' is the NON-induced containment (injective, adjacency-preserving, nothing said about non-edges), which is the source's reading and the one the Bowler-Erde-Heinig-Lehner-Pitz counterexample refutes, while the hypomorphism clause uses INDUCED vertex-deleted subgraphs: x216_del_iso maps the non-v vertices injectively ONTO the non-w vertices and both preserves and reflects adjacency there, and says nothing about f v. x216_hypomorphic is a bijection phi with G - v isomorphic to H - phi(v) for every v, the standard hypomorphism. Both graphs are required infinite (igraph.v's Dedekind infinite_graph: nat injects into the vertices), and the conclusion is the CONJUNCTION 'each embeds in the other', as the source says. The row is disproved upstream and is authored as a refutation target only: no unconditional refutation is committed anywhere in the package (grounding_X216 proves only that Komega does not embed in the edgeless graph and that the two are not hypomorphic).

axv_2506_08810_03.note: Bonamy-Groenland-Johnston-Morrison-Scott Conjecture 24: for every non-transitive finite tournament T there is a countably infinite T-free tournament every locally finite perturbation of which contains an induced copy of T. The finite tournament is a [diGraph] carrying GTBase.common's [tournament]; the countable side is a [rel nat] (the vertex set IS countably infinite by construction). New local vocabulary in X228.v: [x228_ctournament], [x228_transitive], [x228_induced_copy], [x228_lf_perturbation]. The NONEMPTINESS clause of the perturbation (at least one changed pair) is load-bearing: without it the statement would assert both 'R is T-free' and 'R contains T'.

X228:infinite-graph-theory.faithfulness_result: Readback 2026-09-23: 1/1 PASS. axv_2506_08810_03: the nonemptiness clause 'exists x != y with R x y != R' x y' is the source's 'perturbing a NONEMPTY locally finite set of pairs', and it is load-bearing -- without it S is a perturbation of itself and the conjecture would assert both 'S is T-free' and 'S contains T'. 'Locally finite' as 'for each v there is N with R' v u = R v u for all u >= N' is exactly finiteness of the changed set at each vertex on nat, and quantifying it per-vertex (not globally) is right; since both R and R' are tournaments, constraining only the arcs out of v also constrains those into v. x228_induced_copy (injective f with (x -- y) = R (f x) (f y) for distinct x, y) is induced containment, which for tournaments coincides with containment. A relation on nat IS a countably infinite vertex set, so no cardinality layer is needed, and x228_ctournament (irreflexive, exactly one arc between distinct vertices) is the tournament axiom. The non-transitivity guard negates transitivity of the arc relation and is necessary, as the source explains.

bm_025.note: Thomassen's conjecture in the form the book states it (f(k) = 2k): every 2k-connected graph has a spanning k-connected bipartite subgraph. No local vocabulary: [k_connected] is base's Whitney form, [bipartite] base's 2-colouring form, and 'spanning subgraph' is GTBase.common's [del_edge_set G F] (same vertex type, the edges of G outside F), so spanningness is definitional rather than a side condition. Guard [0 < k]: the k = 0 instance is trivially true (delete every edge) and is excluded. The source's partial results (Delcourt-Ferber 2015, Yuster 2024: connectivity O(k^2 log n) suffices) are asymptotic in |V(G)| and are not part of the statement; grounding_X214.v instead grounds the k = 1 instance with an explicit witness (K_3 minus one edge).

bm_046.note: El-Zahar-Erdos (Bondy-Murty A.46): one function f of (r,k), quantified before the graphs, such that chi(G) >= f(r,k) forces either an r-clique or an ANTICOMPLETE pair of vertex sets each of chromatic number exactly k (X3's x3_anticomplete), i.e. an induced subgraph that is the disjoint union of two k-chromatic graphs.

bm_060.note: Vizing's interchange conjecture (Bondy-Murty A.60), corpus status SOLVED (Narboni 2023): from every proper k-edge-colouring a colouring using at most m colours is reachable by Kempe changes, for every achievable m <= k -- which avoids naming chi'(G), the least such m. 'Classes of bounded induced matching treewidth' is modelled by the maximal such classes, fun G => tree_mu_le G m for a fixed m. x220_ibn G t is the induced biclique number, defined relationally (an induced K_{t,t} exists and no induced K_{s,s} with s > t). implications_X220.v records e072 as a candidate and proves the two halves of the dictionary it needs (x220_poly_eval_mono, x220_ibn_free).

axv_2006_09877_00.note: Bonnet-Geniet-Kim-Thomasse-Watrigant Twin-width II, the Small Conjecture. Twin-width is encoded by CONTRACTION SEQUENCES in partition form (x220_twin_width_le): the trigraph reached is determined by the partition, a pair of parts being red exactly when it is neither complete nor anticomplete, the sequence running from the singleton partition to a partition with at most one part (which also covers the empty graph) with red degree always at most d. A class is a Prop on sgraph; hereditary = isomorphism-closed and closed under induced subgraphs; SMALL counts LABELLED graphs, phrased as a bound n! * c^n on the size of every set of adjacency functions on 'I_n realised inside the class, which avoids requiring the class to be decidable. Corpus status DISPROVED (arXiv:2204.12330).

axv_2006_09877_01.note: Same paper, the open question following the Small Conjecture. Polynomial expansion is stated as an edge-density bound on all shallow minors: x220_shallow_minor G H r uses pairwise disjoint branch sets of radius at most r around centres (distance measured INSIDE the branch set by x220_ball_in) and requires only the edges of H to be realised, so a shallow minor may be a subgraph of the contraction, as in the standard definition. The bound is #|E(H)| <= p(r) * #|H| for one polynomial p with natural coefficients.

axv_2001_01607_02.note: Pilipczuk-Sintiari-Thomasse-Trotignon open question: do (triangle, S_{1,2,3})-free graphs have bounded clique-width? Clique-width is encoded by k-EXPRESSIONS (x220_cw_expr: labelled vertex, disjoint union, join of two DISTINCT labels, relabelling), whose denotation is the label list x220_cw_labels e together with the adjacency x220_cw_edge e on positions; a graph is realised when a bijection with the positions is an isomorphism. S_{1,2,3} is the seven-vertex subdivided claw, given by an edge list on 'I_7 through the new el_graph constructor.

axv_2002_00496_02.blocked_reason: Huynh-Joret-Micek-Seweryn-Wollan Conjecture 6 says 'a graph H is unavoidable if and only if H is a minor of some graph from Kelly's construction'. Kelly's construction has NO element-level definition in the source: the paper gives it by Figure 2 and states verbatim that 'its definition for an arbitrary order k can be inferred from the figure'. The equivalent reformulation the paper offers, 'H is a minor of some graph obtained by gluing copies of K_4 along edges in a path-like way, and subdividing all horizontal edges of the K_4s once', is likewise given by a figure (Figure 3) and leaves undetermined both the gluing pattern ('path-like') and which edges of each K_4 are 'horizontal'. No faithful encoding of the right-hand side is therefore available, and approximating it would silently change the conjecture. The LEFT-hand side is fully encoded and faithful: x228_unavoidable H = some threshold d is such that every finite poset whose dimension is not at most d has H as a minor of its cover graph (GTBase.posets). The committed placeholder Definition states the strongest expressible CONSEQUENCE of Conjecture 6, obtained from the two properties the source itself records for Kelly's construction (planar cover graphs of pathwidth 3, both properties minor-closed): every unavoidable graph is Wagner-planar and has treewidth at most 3. Unblocking needs an element-level definition of Kelly's construction taken from the poset-dimension literature.
